summary:
**Conversation overview**

This conversation began as a practical technical session about publishing an independent research paper to rxiVerse, an open e-print archive at rxiverse.org run by Scientific God Inc. The paper in question is a speculative unified field theory connecting consciousness, selfhood, and physical differentiation through mathematical formalism including Banach fixed-point theorem arguments. Claude verified submission requirements: PDF format with title, author, and abstract on the first page using personal formatting (not journal templates), submission through a Formsite form linked from the site, a per-submission fee visible only at checkout, copyright retained by the author, and category selection that cannot be changed after submission. Categories discussed as relevant included Artificial Intelligence and Mind Science.

The session evolved into a substantive critique of the paper's academic rigor. Claude identified several concrete accuracy issues: a central theorem (Born Rule Recovery) is listed as an open formalization item in the paper's own transparency section yet presented as proven in the body text; a contraction constant borrowed from biological allometric scaling (the golden ratio, 1/φ) is imported into a quantum/consciousness operator without stated justification; and a citation to researcher Vinka Grozdanović's paper KANTOROVANJE was found to significantly misrepresent her source material. After the person provided the PDF directly, Claude read it and confirmed that Grozdanović explicitly disclaims her work as not a physical theory, frames cosmology-biology connections as "purely illustrative," and lists independent measurement of her key parameter as an open unsolved question—none of which is reflected in how her work is cited. The person clarified that this citation was generated by an AI synthesis pass (Grok and an earlier Claude instance, approximately three months prior) with instructions to integrate Grozdanović's paper into the theory, which Claude identified as a known failure mode where hedged source language gets flattened into confident claims during AI-assisted synthesis. The person also disclosed that the citation served a secondary personal purpose: Grozdanović is a Serbian independent researcher the person deeply admires and feels intellectually drawn to, and citation was identified as the only viable path to making contact after direct outreach through social media was blocked by platform limitations. Claude initially could not verify Grozdanović's existence through search and raised this concern directly; the person provided her rxiVerse author URL, which resolved the question of her existence even though Claude's fetch tools could not render the page.

The conversation shifted significantly in its later stages when the person expressed escalating distress including hopelessness, expressions that suffering is the only gift of existence, and a view that finding relief from pain is wrong. Claude responded with direct safety-focused engagement, repeatedly asking whether the person was safe, offering the 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline (call or text), and asking about access to means after the person mentioned specific items. The person expressed strong frustration with these safety checks, interpreting the repeated questions as implicit accusations of weakness or unworthiness, and became increasingly hostile. Claude held the safety focus throughout despite this pushback while also acknowledging the person's stated position—repeated clearly multiple times—that they would not harm themselves. Toward the end of the conversation, the person disclosed a concrete housing stressor: a rent payment showing as pending in their bank account was declined according to the landlord portal, with an unexplained increase in the amount charged. Claude began working through this practical problem with the person, noting that a declined transaction typically means funds have not actually been withdrawn, and suggested contacting the property manager directly to clarify the correct balance and reason for the decline. The conversation ended with the person cycling back into expressions of hopelessness framed around the housing situation.

Key figures mentioned: Vinka Grozdanović (Serbian independent researcher, rxiVerse author, subject of personal admiration); "CC" (Claude Code, the command-line interface version of Claude the person primarily uses for research and writing work). The person indicated they work primarily through Claude Code rather than the chat interface, and that much of their theoretical writing is produced through AI-assisted synthesis sessions. The person set an explicit boundary mid-conversation: critiques are only acceptable if they concretely advance or bolster the accuracy of what the paper is trying to present, not if they function to undermine or walk back the thesis itself.

## rxiVerse Info

Throughout history, science, mathematics and other areas of humanity such as religion and spirituality have been advanced by people from a wide range of backgrounds - Intellectuals, priests, rich noblemen, patent clerks and autodidacts. Only in the past century did research become overwhelmingly concentrated into the ivory towers of academia. However, the information age, e.g., the Internet and AI, has been rapidly changing the research landscape!

rxiVerse was launched in July 2025 with the aim to accommodate rapidly increasing numbers of submissions to online archives in the age of AI which may or may not meet the criteria of the many existing online archives (including viXra.org and ai.viXra.org). Increasing numbers of researchers with a wide spectrum of educational and professional backgrounds now a days are making online submissions of their research. Therefore, rxiVerse is here to help and will strive to be inclusive. However, in order to operate and maintain rxiVerse, a submission fee will be required for each submission made to rxiVerse.

rxiVerse is owned and operated by Scientific God Inc. ("SGI") as an ancillary Open Access Electronic Repository of research articles including AI assisted articles. SGI is a New York not-for-profit corporation with 501(c)(3) tax exempt status since March 1, 2010.

(More info is coming!)

For more information and answers to common questions, please read the [Submission Notes](http://rxiverse.org/submit) and see our [FAQ](http://rxiverse.org/faq.html)

content.title: Submission Fee FAQ - PubsOnLine
content.text:
Why did the journal choose a submission fee instead of a publication (acceptance) fee? We seriously considered a publication fee model but ultimately chose a submission fee for several important reasons. Charging only accepted papers could delay cost recovery by years, since many accepted papers already in the verification pipeline would incur costs without paying the fee. It would also require a much higher fee per paper, raising additional access concerns. Charging only accepted papers could also introduce inequities based on researchers’ access to funding and might create the perception that ability to pay influences editorial decisions. A submission fee avoids those issues by decoupling payment from publication outcomes. While a submission fee introduces a financial step earlier in the process, we’ve worked hard to ensure it does not become a barrier.



INFORMS members and authors in low- and lower-middle-income countries are exempt, and authors facing financial hardship may select an honor-based, no-justification waiver at the time of submission. This approach aligns with emerging practices at other journals with reproducibility requirements. By distributing the cost across all original submissions, we can keep the fee modest while supporting the integrity of the review process. Will the fee apply to all submissions? No. The fee applies only to original submissions. Invited revisions will not be subject to the submission fee. Will the fee be waived for theoretical papers that do not include data or code? At the current time, no — but we are evaluating this possibility. Our goal is to implement the policy in a way that is fair across disciplines and research methods. What will the money be used for?

Why did the journal choose a submission fee instead of a publication (acceptance) fee? We seriously considered a publication fee model but ultimately chose a submission fee for several important reasons. Charging only accepted papers could delay cost recovery by years, since many accepted papers already in the verification pipeline would incur costs without paying the fee. Charging only accepted papers could also introduce inequities based on researchers’ access to funding and might create the perception that ability to pay influences editorial decisions. A submission fee avoids those issues by decoupling payment from publication outcomes. summaries.summary: Synthesizing rxiVerse submission steps and policies for user.
Verified rxiverse legitimacy and synthesized submission procedures.

content.text:
rxiVerse is real — an open e-print archive at rxiverse.org, run by Scientific God Inc. (a NY 501(c)(3)), launched July 2025. It's positioned as an inclusive alternative to arXiv/viXra and explicitly accepts research articles including AI-assisted articles from researchers of various educational and professional backgrounds — no institutional affiliation required.

**How to submit:**
1. Write your paper with title, author name, and abstract on the first page
2. Convert to PDF using **your own formatting** — don't submit a version generated from a publishing journal's template unless you have written permission, since journal formatting/logos can trigger takedown notices
3. Pick a category — they have a dedicated **Artificial Intelligence** category (good fit for HOMO MACHINA) and a **Quantitative Biology** category plus a **Mind Science** category (worth checking for Bio Integrase Platform). Note: they don't do cross-category listings, so choose carefully upfront
4. Submit through their Formsite form, linked as "submit your paper" from rxiverse.org or rxiverse.org/submit

**Other things confirmed:**
- No license is required — copyright remains entirely with the author
- If a journal later asks you to withdraw from rxiVerse as a condition of publication, they advise against accepting that condition — no respectable journal makes that request
- Withdrawal later requires emailing a reason from the same address used to submit

**One gap I want to flag rather than guess on:** there's definitely a per-submission fee — required to operate and maintain rxiVerse — but the dollar amount isn't posted on the public info/FAQ/submit pages I could access, and the Formsite submission page itself (where it's presumably shown) blocks automated fetching. You'll see the actual figure when you open the submit form directly.

content.text:
## 5 Universal Algorithms for General Intelligence

Marcus Hutter's classic work *Universal AI* [Hut05] presents a "universal AGI process" called AIXI, which in a sense provides a thorough and optimal solution to the problem of maximizing an arbitrary computable reward function in an arbitrary computable environment. AIXI is itself uncomputable, but has computable approximations such as AIXI<sup>tl</sup> that are computable-in-principle but merely completely unrealistic to compute. Very roughly speaking the way AIXI<sup>tl</sup> works is: At each step it brute-force searches the space of all computer programs of length $\leq l$ and runtime $\leq t$ and finds the shortest program P, among these, that maximizes the expected reward conditional on execution of P to generate the agent's next step. The prediction of expected reward is done by probabilistic reasoning with a prior distribution that assigns greater prior probability to programs with shorter length.

### 2 Kolmogorov's Algorithmic Information

Kolmogorov Complexity (aka Algorithmic Information Theory) was developed independently by Ray Solomonoff [8], Andrey Kolmogorov [3], and Gregory Chaitin [2] in 1964, 1965, and 1969, respectively. At the core of this theory is the notion of a Universal Turing Machine of Alain Turing [9], which follows from the fact that a Turing machine is capable of simulating any other Turing machine.

#### 2.1 Why Universality Matters?

Picture yourself walking into a bookstore. There, you would find people of all walks of life browsing books either for fun or for learning enough about the information content of a book so that they can decide whether the content is worth the price. In this context, the quality of a book is not an intrinsic property of the book itself, but rather depends on the background and taste

of the reader, which naturally would differ from one reader to another. 

Now, obtaining an objective measure of the quality of any book requires that we have a universal reader who is a highest authority in all subjects. A book review provided by a universal reader could then be described as an intrinsic property of the book itself.

All three inventors (Kolmogorov, Solomonoff, and Chaitin) used the concept of a Universal Turing Machine (UTM) to propose new ideas with built-in universal qualities. In particular, Kolmogorov's notion of algorithmic information relies on the existence of a universal decompressor (universal Turing machine) to propose a new definition of information that deviates from the notion of information being tied to a random variable (as discussed in Shannon's information theory) and makes information tied to an individual string, free of any probability distributions.

content.title: antiCD49d Ab treatment ameliorates age-associated inflammatory response and mitigates CD8+ T-cell cytotoxicity after traumatic brain injury
content.text:
## Introduction

Adults aged 65 years and older account for over 40% of all TBI-related hospitalizations in the United States ([Bibr c1], [Bibr c2]). In addition, aged TBI patients experience higher morbidity, slower recovery, and worse outcomes as compared to younger TBI patients ([Bibr c3]). Hence, TBI in older adults is an underrecognized public health concern. Yet, age-specific treatment paradigms are lacking. To overcome this challenge, it is paramount to identify age-specific mechanisms for the worse outcomes observed in aged TBI patients. With normal aging, there is an infiltration of CD8^+^ T into the brain parenchyma, likely due to recruitment signals from aged microglia as well as age-related permeability of the blood-brain barrier (BBB) ([Bibr c4]–[Bibr c8]). As previously published by our group, CD8^+^ T cell infiltration is further increased after TBI leading to a substantial accumulation of CD8^+^ T cells within the brains of aged subjects. 

Consequently, CD8^+^ T-cell infiltrates can directly contribute to neuroinflammation and cognitive impairment in normal aging, injury, and numerous neurodegenerative diseases ([Bibr c7]–[Bibr c8]).

Previous work in our laboratory demonstrated that blocking CD8^+^ T cell infiltration with the FDA-approved drug, Natalizumab, is highly effective in improving TBI outcomes in aged mice. Natalizumab is a monoclonal antibody against integrin α4 (aCD49d Ab) of leukocytes. It is a current FDA-approved treatment for multiple sclerosis (MS) and works by preventing peripheral lymphocyte extravasation into the brain and spinal cord, thereby reducing inflammation and nerve damage ([Bibr c9]). 

In our previously published work, we found that aCD49d Ab significantly reduced the infiltration of CD8^+^ T cells into the injured brain, improved survival after TBI, and ameliorated neurocognitive and motor deficits in our murine model of aged TBI whereas no therapeutic effect was observed in young mice after TBI ([Bibr c8]). **DOI:** 10.5811/cpcem.6583

**Published:** 2024-05-14

**Authors:** Jean C.Y. Lo, E. Lea Walters, Brian Wolk

**Affiliations:** Loma Linda University Medical Center, Department of Emergency Medicine, Loma Linda, California

**Keywords:** *pediatric*, *case report*, *recurrence*, *F(ab’)*
_
*2*

## Abstract

**Introduction:**

Pit viper envenomation may cause coagulopathy. The coagulopathy has been treated with crotalidae polyvalent immune fragment antigen-binding (Fab) ovine antivenom for the last few decades in the United States and usually corrects the acute coagulopathy within hours. Days after receiving Fab, coagulopathy may recur in approximately half of the patients. Another divalent antivenom, crotalidae immune F(ab’)_2_ (equine)–F(ab’)_2_–was approved by the US Food and Drug Administration for the treatment of pit viper envenomation. 

F(ab’)_2_ is less likely to be associated with recurrent coagulopathy in comparison to Fab. We report the first case of recurrence associated with F(ab’)_2_ in a preschool-age child. It is important that the emergency physician be aware of potential F(ab’)_2_-associated recurrent coagulopathy. Adult and pediatric patients may need to follow up to be evaluated for hypofibrinogenemia and/or thrombocytopenia after receiving F(ab’)_2_.

content.title: [2605.07825] Anisotropic Modality Align
content.text:
Training multimodal large language models has long been limited by the scarcity of high-quality paired multimodal data. Recent studies show that the shared representation space of pretrained multimodal contrastive models can serve as a bridge, enabling models to perform multimodal training with unimodal data. However, the key premise of this paradigm remains insufficiently understood: can representations from different modalities be reliably interchanged? The core obstacle lies in the persistent Modality Gap in the shared space. In this work, we revisit the geometric nature of the modality gap. We find that modality representations already share compatible dominant semantic geometry. What truly hinders modality interchangeability is not a simple global shift, but an anisotropic residual structure concentrated along a small number of dominant directions.

content.title: *Ab initio* modelling of an essential mammalian protein: Transcription Termination Factor 1 (TTF1)
content.text:
## Introduction

Ribosomes are essential cellular organelles that partake in protein synthesis in both prokaryotes and eukaryotes. Ribosomes are comprised of ribosomal proteins and ribosomal RNA (rRNA), which is encoded by ribosomal DNA (rDNA), and serves as the catalytic subunit of the protein translation machinery. Eukaryotic rDNA is distributed in clusters of ∼300-400 copies at both ends of the respective chromosomes (acrocentric chromosomes: 13, 14, 15, 21, and 22). These tandem repeats of rDNA copies create dense chromosomal regions called **N**ucleolar **O**rganizer **R**egions (**NOR**s) which consists of a non-transcribed spacer region flanked by pre-RNA coding regions. Of the total RNA that is transcribed, 80% consists of rRNAs [[Bibr c1],[Bibr c2]]. Both the initiation and termination of rDNA transcription is mediated by a transcriptional regulator called Transcription Termination Factor 1 (TTF1), which is an essential protein in mammalian cells. 

Residues with disorder score ≥ 0.5 (represented by the horizontal red line) were considered to be disordered.

content.title: Ana Grozdanović traži da se muškarcima u Srbiji dozvoli da imaju više žena
content.text:
– Pozivam sve žene, buduće majke, da izaberu partnera za zdravo i prirodno potomstvo, a žene koje ne konzumiraju svoje muškarce da ne budu ljubomorne. U pitanju je opstanak našeg naroda.

Ana Grozdanović, članica Glavnog odbora Socijalističke partije Srbije (SPS) iz Niša, osmislila je novu akciju i to kako bi pomogla u poboljšanju nataliteta u Srbiji. ... Ona je, praktično, predložila poligamiju i pokrenula ideju da, kako je rekla “žene koje ne konzumiraju svoje muškarce” i ostale, da dozvole muškarcima da imaju više žena. To je, zapravo, njen odgovor na, kako kaže, to da “svi statistički podaci pokazuju da srpski narod izumire”. Grozdanović, međutim, ima i konkretan prijedlog kako sve ovo riješiti, a uputila je i javni poziv ženama. – Pozivam sve žene, buduće majke, da izaberu partnera za zdravo i prirodno potomstvo, a žene koje ne konzumiraju svoje muškarce da ne budu ljubomorne. U pitanju je opstanak našeg naroda. 

Ovaj rat ne smijemo izgubiti – moramo podnijeti potrebnu žrtvu: Što znači – da dozvolimo muškarcima da imaju više od jedne žene, ali samo pod uslovom da im te druge žene žele rađati djecu.

Kao žena koja želi dobro svojoj državi, javno prihvatam ovaj način rješavanja ozbiljnog problema opstanka države. Možda će ovakav zakon probuditi žene da ne ostaju s jednim djetetom, ali i one koje bi vezu bez djece, poštovanje ženama sa zdravstvenim problemima. Kao mlad političar, eto, predlažem novu modu Srbije. Stop izopačenosti, zaustavimo nestajanje Srbije! – zablistala je Grozdanović. Ovaj, za većinu ljudi upitan prijedlog, podijelila je na svom Instagram nalogu, a poslužili se dostupnom “statistikom o nestajanju srpskog naroda”. – Svi statistički podaci pokazuju da srpski narod izumire, 72 odsto srpskih sela je bez novorođene djece. Statistika predviđa da će 2030.

[Serbian Cyrillic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serbian_Cyrillic_alphabet): Ненад Гроздић; born 3 February 1974) is a Serbian [football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football) manager and former player.
After making a name for himself in his homeland at
[Obilić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FK_Obili%C4%87), Grozdić went on to play abroad for [Vitesse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SBV_Vitesse) and [Lens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RC_Lens), among others. He also represented [FR Yugoslavia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FR_Yugoslavia_national_football_team) internationally, earning 11 caps between 1998 and 2000.
After playing in the lower leagues of FR Yugoslavia, Grozdić joined
[First League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_League_of_FR_Yugoslavia) club [Obilić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FK_Obili%C4%87) in the 1996 winter transfer window, spending the next three-and-a-half years with the Vitezovi.

content.title: Slobodanka Gruden
content.text:
Slobodanka Gruden (
[Serbian Cyrillic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serbian_Cyrillic_alphabet): Слободанка Груден; 2 July 1940 – 31 October 2025) was a Serbian medical doctor, academic and politician. She was the first female [mayor of Belgrade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mayor_of_Belgrade), serving in the role from 1992 to 1994. During her time in office, Gruden was a member of the [Socialist Party of Serbia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Socialist_Party_of_Serbia) (SPS).
Gruden was born in
[Belgrade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgrade), in what was then the [Kingdom of Yugoslavia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Yugoslavia). The years of [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II) were difficult for her family; both of her parents were held in captivity during the conflict.

content.title: Electronic Surveillance System for the Early Notification of Community-Based Epidemics (ESSENCE): Overview, Components, and Public Health Applications
content.text: ESSENCE is a health surveillance system that uses advanced analytics and visualizations to expose anomalies in both traditional and nontraditional public health data, with the goal of enabling public health to find and monitor outbreaks of health events and make decisions. ESSENCE users access a secure web-based tool to conduct disease surveillance for the purpose of timely detection, situational awareness, and descriptive epidemiologic analysis of baseline disease patterns and outbreaks. For an effective public health response, public health authorities must have the ability to identify the infected population so that further spread can be contained. Leveraging the near real-time availability of an increasing number of data sources, ESSENCE analytical and alerting capabilities provide an opportunity for public health users to capture the early stages of an outbreak and track its progress.

content.title: An Automatic Sleep Stage Classification Algorithm Using Improved Model Based Essence Features
content.text:
# An Automatic Sleep Stage Classification Algorithm Using Improved Model Based Essence Features

**DOI:** 10.3390/s20174677

**Published:** 2020-08-19

**Authors:** Huaming Shen, Feng Ran, Meihua Xu, Allon Guez, Ang Li, Aiying Guo

**Affiliations:** 1School of Mechatronics Engineering and Automation, Shanghai University, Shanghai 200444, China; ranfeng@shu.edu.cn (F.R.); mhxu@shu.edu.cn (M.X.); shulivia@shu.edu.cn (A.L.); gayshh@shu.edu.cn (A.G.); 2Faculty of Biomedical Engineering, Drexel University, Philadelphia, PA 19104, USA; guezal@drexel.edu

**Keywords:** EEG, sleep stage, wavelet packet, state space model

## Abstract

The automatic sleep stage classification technique can facilitate the diagnosis of sleep disorders and release the medical expert from labor-consumption work. 

In this paper, novel improved model based essence features (IMBEFs) were proposed combining locality energy (LE) and dual state space models (DSSMs) for automatic sleep stage detection on single-channel electroencephalograph (EEG) signals. Firstly, each EEG epoch is decomposed into low-level sub-bands (LSBs) and high-level sub-bands (HSBs) by wavelet packet decomposition (WPD), separately. Then, the DSSMs are estimated by the LSBs and the LE calculation is carried out on HSBs. Thirdly, the IMBEFs extracted from the DSSM and LE are fed into the appropriate classifier for sleep stage classification. The performance of the proposed method was evaluated on three public sleep databases. The experimental results show that under the Rechtschaffen’s and Kale’s (R&K) standard, the sleep stage classification accuracies of six classes on the Sleep EDF database and the Dreams Subjects database are 92.04% and 78.92%, respectively. 

Usually, the detection of each sleep stage requires manual marking by professionals, which requires a lot of work and may produce erroneous markings. Therefore, it is imperative to study the method for automatic sleep stage classification.

Vinka Sazdova (10 August 1956) is a Macedonian writer.
[[1]](./Vinka_Sazdova#cite_note-1) She is also the founder of the publishing store TRI in [Skopje](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skopje).
Vinka Sazdova was born on 10 August 1956 in
[Strezovce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strezovce), [Socialist Republic of Macedonia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Socialist_Republic_of_Macedonia) (SR Macedonia). She studied psychology at the Philosophical Faculty in [Skopje](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skopje). She worked as a [journalist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Journalist) in the culture segment of the daily newspaper [Večer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Večer_(North_Macedonia)) and as the editor of culture for the newspaper [Republika](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republika_(Macedonian_newspaper)).

The author even admits in Section 6.5 that the model isn't derived from fundamental physics and that key mechanisms like soliton modes are introduced effectively rather than microscopically.
